review_kind: Codex AI narrow read-only independent N703 source/test-contract peer review

checks.observed_source: remove_install validates each top-level installer path with _refusal, then _delete removes the complete allowed root. With no keep descendant, it uses rmtree. With explicit keep paths, it recursively removes siblings without calling _refusal again for each child. Windows passes only the current install log, icon and NSIS status file to --keep before staging.
checks.qualification: This is not deletion of every arbitrary directory: shared/user-data/running/source-checkout and ownership guards still apply. It describes an allowed discovered installer root. Existing root/cache and root/test_data are not default keep entries unless another existing guard or explicit keep protects them.
checks.test_contract: test_install_cleanup windows_online builds cache/wheels/w.whl; test_every_released_layout_is_found_and_removed_down_to_user_data expects only separate Box.user_files after removal. test_the_log_of_the_new_install_is_kept_while_the_old_copy_goes demonstrates explicit keep sparing the log, not preserving all runtime-root caches.

checks.observed_source: Normal _user_data includes standard ~/.spacr, XDG spaCR data/cache/config/state and HF_HOME or its fallback. It does not enumerate custom SPACR_HOME, CELLPOSE_LOCAL_MODELS_PATH, SPACR_BACKENDS_DIR or _relocated_caches. Some of those appear in separate opt-in _purge_targets, which does not make them normal preservation entries.
checks.qualification: For a known protected _user_data location, _refusal checks overlap both ways. A known protected folder nested inside an installer root refuses the whole root before recursive deletion; the same folder is not silently deleted merely because child recursion omits _refusal. The gap concerns configured/relocated locations absent from the normal protected list or explicit keep. An external configured folder outside the deleted root is not deleted by this path.
checks.future_test_scope: Place each configured persistent directory inside and outside an otherwise allowed root, plus known HF/XDG protected descendant controls and explicit nested keep. Assert byte preservation and accurately reported refusal/remaining runtime. Symlink/junction/native filesystem behavior needs separate platform tests, not assumed from lexical _inside.

checks.observed_source: PowerShell obtains its temporary bootstrap/Python first, then invokes cleanup remove before creating/installing/validating StageVenv. pip check and isolated imports occur later. Only after those checks does it move any surviving VenvDir to .venv-previous, activate StageVenv and immediately delete .venv-previous. Catch cleans StageVenv/StageProfile and rethrows; it does not restore a removed old root or move a surviving previous environment back.
checks.qualification: An earlier bootstrap/download failure leaves cleanup unexecuted. A root refused by known data guards may retain its old runtime until later activation. When cleanup actually removed the allowed old root and later dependency/staging validation fails, .venv-previous cannot recover that already deleted environment. This is not a reproduced Windows failure or proof that every failed upgrade destroys the old runtime.
checks.test_contract: test_install_is_validated_before_the_previous_environment_is_replaced is static text ordering: pip check/import before the first venv-previous occurrence. It does not compare those checks with the earlier CleanupModule remove call. test_the_update_finds_then_deletes_then_installs explicitly asserts delete before install; failure helper test checks no relaunch after installer error but does not prove old-runtime preservation/rollback.
checks.future_test_scope: Inject failure after cleanup, dependency installation, pip check/import, activation move and first GUI launch. Require old verified runtime plus cache/user data to remain available until new runtime and actual GUI acceptance succeed, and prove rollback restores owned links/runtime without deleting persistent data.

acceptance_boundaries: Reading source and assertions confirms current policy and test limits; no fresh tests passed in this peer review.
Windows native installer execution, failure recovery, junctions/locked files, shortcut registration and actual GUI version/import identity remain unverified here.
Staged import validation and installer exit zero are not native GUI acceptance.
No broad N703 source sweep or other owner claims were re-audited.
future_policy_direction: Stage and verify a new owned runtime before retiring the old owned runtime; keep persistent cache/data and unknown user files by default. Retain rollback material until actual new-GUI acceptance. This is proposed repair scope, not an implemented guarantee.
